inline_comments.comment: The documented default is `true`, but the actual default set in `common-preset.ts` is `false`, and the JSDoc `@default` tag in `core-common.ts` also says `false`. This contradicts the behavior users will observe and will cause confusion. Change this to `Default: \`false\``.

A `TODO` comment inside a public-facing JSDoc block will surface directly in IDE tooltips for anyone configuring their `main.ts`. End-users shouldn't see internal release-planning notes. Track this as a GitHub issue instead and remove the TODO from the JSDoc.

The immediately preceding flag, `experimentalCodeExamples`, carries an `@experimental` tag to signal to users that the feature may change. Since `changeDetection` defaults to `false` and has an explicit TODO to flip the default before the 10.4 release (implying it is not yet stable/finished), adding `@experimental This feature is in early development and may change significantly in future releases.` would be consistent with that established pattern and set appropriate user expectations.

"Enable change detection." is the entire description. Every other flag section in this file provides meaningful context — what the feature does, what addon or UI surface it controls, and often a link to further documentation. Change detection is a non-obvious term for a Storybook user; even a single sentence explaining what is being detected (e.g., story or component changes between renders/runs) would significantly improve discoverability and usability.

general_comments.comment: The feature flag is defined and given a default value, but no code in this diff (or, based on a search of the repository, anywhere currently reachable) actually reads `features.changeDetection` to gate any behavior. Other flags like `componentsManifest` are immediately consumed (e.g., `if (features?.componentsManifest) { registerManifests(...) }`). As submitted, toggling this flag has no observable effect, making it dead configuration. If the consuming implementation is intentionally landing in a follow-up PR, that should be called out explicitly in the PR description so reviewers can evaluate completeness.
